messages:
cassie: Heads-up — running a preemptible eviction simulation tomorrow 2025-10-18 17:00 UTC (10:00 PDT). Scope: us-west1 + eu-west1 mixed pools. Goal: validate failover to dedicated/on-demand, autoscaler behavior, and job retry semantics. :rocket:

oliver: +1. what's the blast radius? how many nodes?

cassie: Planning to evict 8 GPU nodes total (4 per region). We'll target a canary set first (2 nodes/region) then escalate if healthy.

anya: Can you drop the runbook here? I can own the observability dashboard during the run.

mike: Runbook (short):
- Prep: enable feature flag `preemptible-sim=true` on infra staging and prod-canary.
- Canary: evict 2 nodes in us-west1, wait 10m, observe error rates + autoscaler.
- Scale: if canary OK, evict remaining nodes in region. Repeat for eu-west1.
- Rollback: cancel eviction + uncordon nodes, failover traffic back to dedicated pool.

Commands we'll run:```bash
# simulate preemption on a GKE node (cordon + evict pods)
kubectl cordon gpu-node-abc
kubectl drain gpu-node-abc --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# for k8s batch jobs we also patch the node to simulate preemptible taint
kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-abc preemptible=true:NoSchedule
```

natalie: Observability checklist (I'll monitor):
- API p95, p99 latency (per-route + overall)
- Token throughput and per-token cost spike
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) and user-visible failures
- Autoscaler events (scale up/down, failed attempts)
- Eviction/restart counts for workers + job retry latencies
- KV cache hit ratio and cold-start token penalty

evict-bot: scheduled eviction job 1762155400 started for canary nodes in us-west1. Target nodes: gpu-canary-01,gpu-canary-02.

oncall-sre: I'm on watch for the run. If we see >1% user-facing errors for 5m we abort. Also watching inter-region egress to avoid cross-region data spikes. :eyes:

oliver: Quick question — for mixed pools, what's our fallback order? (1) cached responses, (2) dedicated pool, (3) queue + retry?

mike: Fallback policy: 1) route to same-model dedicated variant in same region (if available), 2) if capacity not available, route to nearest region dedicated (respecting data residency tags), 3) if still unavailable, apply short client-side retry (exponential, max 3) and queue request to worker pool. We want to avoid cross-region unless necessary.

anya: Success criteria proposed:
- User-visible error rate <= 1% sustained during evictions
- P95 latency <= 2x baseline for at most 3 minutes after an eviction burst
- Autoscaler scales to required capacity within 90s for 90% of events
- No more than 5% of traffic served cross-region in steady state
- Jobs that are retried should succeed within 3 attempts 95% of the time

natalie: Metrics to capture for postmortem:
- time-to-first-byte delta per route
- percent requests hitting cached prefixes vs cold KV misses
- GPU utilization and queue length per pod
- cost delta (estimated $/token) during the window

cassie: If we hit an unexpected failure pattern we stop and run the failback plan. Postrun owner: @natalie for metrics, @anya for customer impact analysis, @mike for infra changes.

oliver: small mitigation we should verify: tenant routing respects `avoid-preemptible` flag on high-SLA customers and they never go to preemptible pool.

mike: Will add a quick pre-check to ensure no high-SLA route is routed into the canary preemptible pool.

evict-bot: canary eviction complete for us-west1 (2 nodes). Pods drained: 82. Restarted: 78. Autoscaler triggered scale-up: +6 pods.

oncall-sre: Observing p95 increased ~1.4x for 90s, errors at 0.6% — within thresholds. Moving to region-scale step in 10m.

cassie: Reminder: keep interrupts in 2 waves, give autoscaler time. If dedicated pool saturates, we want clear signals to stop.

oliver: Noted. Also be mindful of stateful jobs — ensure graceful checkpointing.

mike: After region runs, we'll run a short spike test: artificially double arrival rate for 5m to test cost/latency tradeoffs.

anya: Thanks all. I'll update the runbook doc with these criteria and tag the postmortem template. See you tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
